question: What is the primary reason topical administration is preferred for eye conditions?

options.A: Systemic medications take too long to swallow
options.B: The blood-ocular barrier restricts systemic drugs
options.C: Topical drops are cheaper to manufacture
options.D: The eye has no blood supply of its own

explanation: Tight junctions in the eye prevent most systemic drugs from entering, making direct topical application necessary. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h1)

question: How can eye drops intended for local use end up causing systemic side effects?

options.A: Absorption through the nasolacrimal duct into circulation
options.C: Direct penetration through the hard outer cornea
options.D: Inhalation of the vapor during blinking

explanation: Excess eye drops drain into the nasal mucosa and enter systemic blood vessels, bypassing first-pass metabolism. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h1)

question: Which class of glaucoma medication can cause permanent brown pigmentation of the iris?
explanation: Latanoprost and similar prostaglandin analogues gradually increase melanin in the iris over months of use. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h2)

question: A patient with a history of bronchial asthma is prescribed eyedrops for glaucoma. Which drug class must the nurse question if ordered?
explanation: Systemic absorption of topical beta-blockers like timolol can trigger severe bronchospasm in asthmatic patients. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h2)

question: What is the primary action of a cycloplegic drug on the eye?

options.A: Paralyzes the ciliary muscle and blocks accommodation
options.B: Numbs the surface of the cornea
options.C: Increases the drainage of aqueous humor
options.D: Constricts the pupil for intraocular surgery

explanation: Cycloplegics relax the ciliary body so the lens cannot focus for close reading or near vision work. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h3)

question: Why do patients receiving eye drops that cause mydriasis often complain of bright sunlight?

options.A: The retina becomes hypersensitive to electrical impulses
options.B: The drug destroys the pigmented cells of the iris
options.C: Tear production stops completely and dries the surface
options.D: The pupil remains dilated and lets in excess light

explanation: With the iris sphincter paralyzed or radial muscle overstimulated, the pupil cannot constrict in bright light. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h3)

question: What is a major complication associated with the long-term use of ophthalmic corticosteroids?

options.B: Total loss of the corneal epithelium

explanation: Prolonged steroid use in the eye raises intraocular pressure and promotes lens opacity formation. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h4)

question: Why is patient adherence critical when dispensing antibiotic eye drops for bacterial conjunctivitis?

options.A: Incomplete courses cause permanent damage to the optic nerve
options.B: Leftover drops will crystallize inside the conjunctival sac
options.C: Microorganisms multiply faster once treatment begins
options.D: Stopping early can lead to recurrent infection and drug resistance

explanation: Failing to finish antibiotics allows surviving bacteria to multiply and develop resistance to the treatment. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h4)

question: What is the clinical purpose of instilling fluorescein sodium dye into the eye?

options.A: To measure the exact intraocular pressure
options.B: To treat acute bacterial conjunctivitis infections
options.C: To highlight corneal abrasions under specialized light
options.D: To paralyze the ciliary muscle during refraction

explanation: Fluorescein stains areas where the corneal epithelium is damaged, making abrasions glow green under cobalt blue light. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h5)

question: A patient receives a topical anesthetic for a corneal foreign body removal. What instruction must the nurse give before discharge?

options.A: Wash the eye immediately with clean salty water
options.B: Apply a tight pressure bandage for two hours
options.C: Return tomorrow if the vision becomes blurry
options.D: Do not rub the eye while the numbness persists

explanation: Anesthetized corneas cannot feel pain, making it easy for the patient to accidentally scratch or ulcerate the surface by rubbing. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h5)

question: What is the primary function of a cerumenolytic ear drop?

options.A: To soften and break up impacted earwax
options.B: To dry up excessive fluid drainage from otitis
options.C: To numb the tympanic membrane for surgery
options.D: To kill bacterial pathogens in the middle ear

explanation: Cerumenolytics break down hard earwax so it can be safely removed from the external auditory canal. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h6)

question: Why is checking the integrity of the tympanic membrane crucial before giving certain ear drops?

options.A: The eardrum absorbs the active drug into the brain
options.B: Pressure from the drops will rupture the cochlea instantly
options.C: Medications can enter the middle ear and cause ototoxicity
options.D: Drops will evaporate too quickly if the membrane is open

explanation: An open eardrum allows otic drops to reach delicate inner ear structures, potentially causing hearing loss or severe vertigo. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h6)

question: How should the nurse pull the pinna when administering ear drops to an adult patient?
explanation: Pulling the adult pinna upward and backward straightens the external auditory canal for proper drop instillation. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h7)

question: What action should the nurse perform immediately after instilling eye drops to reduce systemic drug absorption?

options.A: Flush the conjunctiva with normal saline solution
options.B: Ask the patient to blink rapidly ten times
options.C: Press gently on the inner corner of the eye
options.D: Wipe the eyelids firmly with a sterile dry gauze

explanation: Punctal occlusion blocks the tear duct temporarily, keeping the medication in the eye and stopping drainage into nasal blood vessels. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h7)

question: What is the primary danger of touching the tip of an eye drop bottle to the eyelashes?

options.A: It causes the active chemical ingredients to separate
options.B: It bends the dropper nozzle and blocks the fluid
options.C: It neutralizes the pH balance of the sterile liquid
options.D: It contaminates the remaining solution with microorganisms

explanation: Contact with skin or lashes transfers bacteria into the bottle, turning the medication into a source of infection. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h8)

question: Why must nurses advise patients never to share personal eye drops with family members?

options.A: Shared bottles run out of medication twice as fast
options.B: It can easily spread bacterial or viral eye infections
options.C: Different family members always have mismatched eye colors
options.D: Prescription drugs change composition when used by two people

explanation: Pathogens from an infected eye can contaminate the dispenser tip and infect the next person who uses the bottle. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h8)
